## Startup and shutdown

[`auto_open`](https://github.com/statisticsnorway/nadabas/blob/3b4c05386e5a44d05633136ecbcf5dd067f70435/vba/modules/AutoOpenClose.bas#L26)
is the add-in startup entry point.

```{mermaid}
sequenceDiagram
  participant Excel
  participant Startup as "AutoOpenClose.auto_open"
  participant Language as "MultiLang"
  participant Events as "AppEvents"
  participant State as "Globals and RibbonUI"
  participant Registry as "InterfaceRegistry"
  participant Database as "Database settings"
  participant Release as "GitHub releases"

  Excel->>Startup: Open NADABAS workbook or add-in
  Startup->>Language: LoadLanguage
  Startup->>Startup: Detect add-in or developer-file mode
  Startup->>Events: Create and bind AppEvents to Application
  Startup->>State: Initialize sleeping state, collections, DB objects, settings
  Startup->>Registry: GetDBSettings and GetSatelliteSettings
  Startup->>State: Reset menu, batch, year, and conversion flags
  Excel->>Database: Open NADABAS database
  Database->>State: Load administrator and shared user settings
  State->>Release: Schedule delayed weekly release check when enabled
```

The source performs these steps:

1. Load localized text collections.
2. Set add-in/development-mode flags and, for a NADABAS workbook opened as a
   normal file, disable an installed NADABAS add-in to reduce conflicts.
3. Show the language dialog when running as a normal development file.
4. Create `AppEvents` and bind its `App` member to Excel's `Application`.
5. Mark NADABAS as sleeping; create `WBDataColl`, `BaseDb`, `ExchDB`, and user
   settings; clear administrator and false-user state.
6. Load base and satellite database definitions from the Windows registry.
7. Reset menu selection, batch, year, and file-conversion flags.
8. When a database is opened, load its shared settings and schedule a release
   check five seconds later when the administrator-controlled setting is on and
   no check has been attempted in the last seven days.

The update check is scheduled through `Application.OnTime` after database
startup. It sends a read-only HTTPS `GET` request with a NADABAS-specific
user-agent and short per-phase timeouts, then compares the numeric components
of the release tag with `dlgAbout.VersionNumber`. A newer version changes the
existing About ribbon label; the About dialog shows installed/latest version
information and links users to the familiar NADABAS download page at
<https://nadabas.net/nadabas/documents-and-downloads>. GitHub remains the
technical source for the latest published version number. There is no modal
startup message and the check never downloads or installs a file.

The database-wide `UserSettings.CheckForUpdates` value defaults to enabled and
can only be changed from the administrator ribbon menu. Current versions,
missing releases, offline use, proxy failures, and malformed responses remain
silent. The last-attempt day and last successfully observed public version are
cached in the current user's `NADABAS\VersionUpdate` registry settings so the
passive About indicator survives Excel sessions between weekly checks.

[`auto_close`](https://github.com/statisticsnorway/nadabas/blob/3b4c05386e5a44d05633136ecbcf5dd067f70435/vba/modules/AutoOpenClose.bas#L101)
cancels a pending delayed release check so Excel does not call back into an
add-in that has already closed. Other shutdown cleanup remains **unknown**.

## Application events

[`AppEvents.cls`](https://github.com/statisticsnorway/nadabas/blob/3b4c05386e5a44d05633136ecbcf5dd067f70435/vba/classes/AppEvents.cls)
subscribes to Excel application events.

| Event | Source behaviour | Runtime checks still required |
|---|---|---|
| `App_NewWorkbook` | Adds a `clsWBData` entry keyed by full workbook name. | Duplicate and unsaved-workbook names. |
| `App_WorkbookOpen` | Adds or reuses workbook state; scans `DBLinks` and optional `ExchLinks`; when a database is active, matches registered workbook name and path and applies read-only/protection state. | Permissions, reservations, path casing, and externally opened files. |
| `App_WorkbookActivate` | Selects current workbook state, invalidates the ribbon, finds `DBLinks`, and hides template sheets for non-administrators. | Multi-window and protected-workbook behaviour. |
| `App_SheetChange` | If active and change tracking is enabled, finds workbook state and marks it dirty only when `wbExchHasPut` is true. | Whether base-database `PUTDB` changes should also mark dirty. |
| `App_WorkbookBeforeClose` | Removes session state, optionally tests dirty data, may offer to free the current user's reservation, and turns tracing off for a trace workbook. | Cancelled close, error paths, and settings combinations. |
| `App_WorkbookBeforeSave` | Removes the workbook password for Save As, optionally saves descriptions, blocks protected workbook saves, and clears session dirty state. | Failed save and password-policy behaviour. |
| `App_WorkbookAfterSave` | When the full name changed, rekeys `clsWBData` and marks the saved-as workbook unregistered. | Save As failure and concurrent event order. |

::: {.callout-warning title="Dirty-state verification point"}
The retained draft described change tracking as applying to a workbook that
saves data. The exported handler specifically tests `wbExchHasPut`, not
`wbHasPut`. This may be intentional exchange-only behaviour or a defect. Do not
generalize it in requirements until an Excel test and maintainer decision are
recorded.
:::

## Ribbon state and callbacks

[`RibbonUI.bas`](https://github.com/statisticsnorway/nadabas/blob/3b4c05386e5a44d05633136ecbcf5dd067f70435/vba/modules/RibbonUI.bas)
must keep its module name because ribbon XML refers to it. It maintains the
`IRibbonUI` reference, current workbook state, the `WBDataColl` collection, and
callbacks used by Excel.

Callback responsibilities fall into three groups:

| Group | Examples | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| State callbacks | `Enabled...`, `Visible...`, `...State` | Decide whether a control is enabled, visible, or pressed from database, administrator, workbook, and named-range state. |
| Text callbacks | `CommonGetLabel`, `AboutGetLabel` | Resolve translated labels from the ribbon language collection and select the passive update label when needed. |
| Action callbacks | `...Click`, `LoadData`, `SaveData`, `OpenCloseDB` | Capture the active workbook where needed and dispatch to command modules or forms. |

`SetNadabasIsSleeping`, `SetCurrentWBData`, and collection update routines call
`DoInvalidateIf`, which asks Excel to redraw ribbon state. `TestGetAndPut` and
`TestExchGetAndPut` scan the last column of the relevant named range. Recognized
load modes include `GETDB`, `GETTEMP`, `GETINFO`, and `LOADDB`; `PUTDB` enables
save capability; `MIXED` enables both.

## Session state

The most widely shared state is declared in
[`Globals.bas`](https://github.com/statisticsnorway/nadabas/blob/3b4c05386e5a44d05633136ecbcf5dd067f70435/vba/modules/Globals.bas).

| Variable | Type or role | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `NadabasIsSleeping` | Boolean | No database is active; change through `SetNadabasIsSleeping` so the ribbon is invalidated. |
| `WBDataColl` | `Collection` of `clsWBData` | Per-open-workbook UI and workflow state, keyed by full name. |
| `Databases` | `Collection` of `clsDB` | Base database definitions loaded from the registry. |
| `SatelliteDBs` | `Collection` of `clsDB` | Optional satellite definitions loaded from the registry. |
| `CurrentDB` | `clsDB` | Database currently used by shared routines. |
| `BaseDb`, `ExchDB`, `SatelliteDB` | `clsDB` | Database-role objects. |
| `Usersettings` | `clsUserSettings` | Settings loaded from or saved to the current database. |
| `isAdministrator` | Boolean | Result of the administrator-table check for the current user. |
| `DescriptionRange`, `DBGlobalsRange` | Excel `Range` | Named-range pointers used by description and global-value workflows. |
| `NADABASISNOTADDIN`, `NADABASINADDINMODE` | Boolean | Development-file and add-in-mode flags. |

`clsWBData` records the full workbook name, named-range capabilities,
registration, reservation, transfer/export, read-only/protected state, and the
NADABAS dirty flag. It is session state, not an authoritative replacement for
the `Workbooks` table or Excel's own saved state.

## Forms and module conventions

The export shows useful conventions, but they are not absolute API rules:

| Prefix | Observed role |
|---|---|
| `dlg` | Modal dialogs for selection, confirmation, input, or status. |
| `frm` | Functional forms, commonly paired with a `cmd...` module. |
| `Splash` | Modeless progress or status forms used during long operations. |
| `uf` | UserForms used by legacy workbook-conversion flows. |
| `cmd` | Ribbon-facing command and orchestration modules. |
| `Interface` | Windows, file, registry, shell, web, or dialog integration. |
| `cls` | Domain, state, data-access, settings, or UI helper classes. |

Form behaviour may live in both the `.frm` file and its invoking module. Binary
`.frx` resources must remain paired with their `.frm` source during export,
review, and import.

## Active workbook references

Many command procedures copy `Application.ActiveWorkbook` or a helper result
into a local `awb` variable and pass it onward. This reduces reliance on a
global active-workbook value changing while forms, add-in windows, or newly
opened workbooks receive focus. It is a convention, not a guarantee: reviewers
should still trace every workflow that opens or activates another workbook.
